description.narrative: (Lebanon): The Water Sanitation and Conservation (WSC) flagship water sector activity continues USAID's partnership with the four Lebanese Regional Water Establishments (RWEs) and the Litani River Authority (LRA) by expanding the capacity of potable water pumping and wastewater treatment facilities, increasing the efficiency of public water utilities to manage water services, and supporting communities and the private sector to promote effective water stewardship among citizens. WSC will invest in innovative solutions that promote water conservation, energy efficiency, and cost recovery. Using FY 2024 resources, USAID will implement targeted interventions to enhance water and wastewater infrastructure, integrate renewable energy for efficient water distribution, and promote sustainable water management, all closely aligned with the Ministry of Energy and Water's strategy and USAID's development objectives in the water sector. These initiatives include completing renewable energy systems for water supply benefitting 392,000 people, finalizing system designs to be initiated in the upcoming fiscal year, and improving water operations through performance-based contracts, and introducing industrial water reuse practices. Support for RWEs will strengthen management tools, business continuity planning, and revenue collection while developing emergency plans - a source of resilience in a crisis-prone country. WSC will also be exploring possibilities of interventions that can address the needs in the Southern and Bekaa areas affected by fighting between Hizballah and Israel. Additionally, USAID will expand civic engagement by empowering civil society organizations to promote water conservation practices by launching awareness campaigns, and facilitating municipal agreements focused on conservation and efficiency billing and collection, and facility maintenance. These efforts will improve water-use efficiency and ensure sustainable resource management..
